verdictRationale: The prior severe UPDATE_POLICY.md issue is satisfied: v2 now makes policy parsing deterministic and fail-closed. Two new enforceability problems remain around digest canonicalization and registry merge verification, both fixable but important before implementation.

falsifiability.failureCondition: A manifest containing manifest_digest and signature fields cannot be validated consistently because the spec does not define the canonical byte range over which the digest is computed.
falsifiability.observableSignal: Two conforming implementations compute different manifest digests for the same manifest or one implementation cannot produce a manifest whose embedded digest validates.
falsifiability.measurementMethod: Create a sample manifest with manifest_digest and signature populated, run two independent canonicalization routines against the full JSON and against JSON with verification fields removed, and compare validation outcomes.
falsifiability.threshold: Exactly one normative digest algorithm and excluded-field set must validate across implementations.

newIssueList.title: Manifest digest canonicalization is underspecified
newIssueList.description: The manifest includes `manifest_digest` inside the JSON whose digest it claims to represent, and also has an optional `signature` field. The spec does not define whether the digest covers the full manifest, excludes `manifest_digest`, excludes `signature`, or uses a canonical JSON serialization. Under adversarial reading, manifest verification can become impossible or implementation-specific while still satisfying the prose.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: Define a canonical manifest verification payload, such as RFC 8785 canonical JSON with `manifest_digest` and `signature` omitted before hashing. Require all digest and signature verification to use that exact canonical payload.

newIssueList.title: Registry merge content digest conflicts with local additions
newIssueList.description: `merge_registry_additive` requires a `content_digest` described as the post-merge content digest, but additive registry merging is supposed to preserve existing local entries. If a customer registry already contains allowed local additions, the final post-merge file digest cannot be known by the canonical manifest unless the manifest also knows every local registry state. This creates pressure either to reject safe local additions or to overwrite them, both contrary to the safety model.
newIssueList.suggestedFix: For additive registry merges, define verification over the artifact patch plus deterministic merge invariants rather than a single manifest-known full-file digest, or require `content_digest` to mean the digest of the canonical added fragment only for merge operations.
newIssueList.lineRef: Update Manifest / files[].content_digest and Update Plan Generation / merge_registry_additive

ledgerReview.rationale: The files[] manifest model and plan traceability requirements remain explicit and enforceable.
Missing or ambiguous customer policy now clearly fails closed for apply.
The approval artifact is concrete and bound to install, manifest, plan, operation ids, and expiry.
Path safety is now stated as a repeated planning and write-time invariant.
The new frontmatter schema, enum rules, duplicate-field invalidation, and policy digest re-gate close the machine-enforceability gap.

preserveList.summary: The spec correctly limits auto-apply to explicit manifest-backed operations with local file-state proof.
The policy model now treats human prose as non-enforceable and fails closed on missing or unparsable frontmatter.
The heartbeat allowlist and fail-closed telemetry violation behavior give a concrete privacy enforcement point.
